title: Mughal Conquest of Chittagong
subtitle: Mughal forces end Arakanese control and incorporate Chittagong.
summary: In 1666, Mughal forces under the Bengal administration captured Chittagong from Arakanese control after coordinated land-naval operations. The conquest integrated a strategic port frontier into Mughal Bengal.
heroTagline: Chittagong's capture secured Bengal's southeastern maritime frontier for the Mughals.
whyItMatters: This event matters because it expanded provincial control to a key coastal node, reducing frontier instability and strengthening maritime-security governance.
longTermLegacy: The annexation of Chittagong improved the coherence of Bengal's territorial administration and reshaped long-term coastal governance dynamics.
identityMemoryNotes: In Bengal's memory, 1666 marks a turning point in securing the southeastern frontier and linking delta governance to Bay-facing strategy.
